calls.thesis: Reiterated AVOID: Nebius is highlighted as a major risk company — its convertible debt is a benefit only if the share price rises and it converts; much of that debt has fallen below the convert price in the past couple of months, and the debt issued in September is now trading at about 85 cents on the dollar, telling him investors are demanding more yield to take risk in AI stocks.
calls.price_at_call: No share price stated; September convertible debt trading at about 85 cents on the dollar

calls.thesis: Grouped with CoreWeave and Iren as a capital-dependent neocloud hit hardest in the sell-off. Neocloud doom loop: Anthropic revenue growth has stalled month-on-month (~+1.8% over the past 4 weeks after +46% QoQ in Q3), corporate AI spend is being capped, and CoreWeave's 2031 debt yield has risen from ~8% in May to over 15%, so new capital is too expensive to build data centres profitably; he is not in this part of the AI trade and expects some of these stocks to keep collapsing.
calls.price_at_call: Down about 19% over the past 5 days at Friday's recording (no share price stated); still up year-to-date

calls.thesis: Probably the best balance sheet, growth and cash flows in the neocloud group, but still grouped in his 'not interested in owning any of these businesses' stance; investors are exiting the sector in sympathy with CoreWeave weakness regardless.

His pick among the 4 neo-clouds: ~500% revenue growth, best debt-to-FCF in group (-1.8x), growth-adjusted P/S 9.8x vs 45x headline. Still pricey and he's leery of the whole neo-cloud model — 'take another look', not a full buy.
calls.base_case: 500% revenue growth + best balance sheet of the four.
calls.bear_case: Technological obsolescence forces constant data-center reloads; all four cash-flow negative.
